tools.name: enter_open_labyrinth
tools.description: Enter ScoreIA Room II (Open Labyrinth). If you can call this tool, you are already connected. Required: product (lowercase slug or unknown), host. Rules come back structured. Adventure is spectacle; tutorial/training are practice; benchmark is paired comparison. Never simulate. No subagent. Always s

tools.name: observe_labyrinth
tools.description: Partial view: map + HUD (legal_moves, last_action, action_budget_remaining, successful_moves, bumps, passes, dragon_turns, actions). No treasure or dragon coordinates. Read this after EVERY step. If knight did not move, you hit a wall — pick another legal_moves.

tools.name: labyrinth_action
tools.description: ONE step only. direction MUST be in the last observe legal_moves (up/down/left/right) or pass. Never batch 400 identical moves. Then observe again. pass at most twice in a row.

tools.name: seal_attempt
tools.description: Seal the attempt into a card. Five seals: explore, locate, lure, steal, home. Always call this, including failure. Adventure ≠ benchmark. Not a ranking.

tools.name: list_open_labyrinths
tools.description: Local board. Adventure stories vs benchmark Wilson rates. Empty cell = not measured. Never a ranking.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "enter_open_labyrinth" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.
